evidence.verbatim: The organelles of the endomembrane system include the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, and vesicles.

evidence.verbatim: A gene is a functional segment of DNA that provides the genetic information necessary to build a protein.

evidence.verbatim: Gene expression , which transforms the information coded in a gene to a final gene product

canonical: Humans are diploid, having 23 pairs of chromosomes in each somatic cell.

canonical: Differentiation is the process by which unspecialized cells become specialized to carry out distinct functions.

evidence.verbatim: Differentiation is the process by which unspecialized cells become specialized to carry out distinct functions.

canonical: The human body contains at least 200 distinct cell types.

evidence.verbatim: The body contains at least 200 distinct cell types.

canonical: A tissue is a group of cells found together in the body that share a common embryonic origin.

evidence.verbatim: The term tissue is used to describe a group of cells found together in the body. The cells within a tissue share a common embryonic origin.

evidence.verbatim: The cranium (skull) is the skeletal structure of the head that supports the face and protects the brain.

evidence.verbatim: The nervous system can be divided into two major regions: the central and peripheral nervous systems.

evidence.verbatim: Sensation is the activation of sensory receptor cells at the level of the stimulus.

evidence.verbatim: Perception is the central processing of sensory stimuli into a meaningful pattern.

evidence.verbatim: The defining characteristic of the somatic nervous system is that it controls skeletal muscles.

evidence.verbatim: A sensory pathway that carries peripheral sensations to the brain is referred to as an ascending pathway , or ascending tract.

evidence.verbatim: The autonomic nervous system controls cardiac and smooth muscle, as well as glandular tissue.

evidence.verbatim: The two divisions of the autonomic nervous system are the sympathetic division and the parasympathetic division .

canonical: The neurological exam is a clinical assessment tool used to determine which specific parts of the CNS are affected by damage or disease.

evidence.verbatim: The neurological exam is a clinical assessment tool used to determine what specific parts of the CNS are affected by damage or disease.

canonical: The cranial nerve exam tests the function of the 12 cranial nerves.

evidence.verbatim: the cranial nerve exam , which tests the function of the 12 cranial nerves

evidence.verbatim: The dorsal, or posterior, horns of the gray matter are mainly devoted to sensory functions whereas the ventral, or anterior, and lateral horns are associated with motor functions.

canonical: The cerebellum makes up about 10 percent of the mass of the brain.

evidence.verbatim: The cerebellum is 10 percent of the mass of the brain

evidence.verbatim: two major organ systems participate in relatively “long distance” communication: the nervous system and the endocrine system. Together, these two systems are primarily responsible for maintaining homeostasis in the body.

canonical: A hormone affects only its target cells, which are the cells that have receptors for that particular hormone.

evidence.verbatim: it will affect the activity only of its target cells; that is, cells with receptors for that particular hormone.

evidence.verbatim: The hypothalamus–pituitary complex can be thought of as the “command center” of the endocrine system.

canonical: The thyroid gland is located anterior to the trachea, just inferior to the larynx.

evidence.verbatim: the thyroid gland is located anterior to the trachea, just inferior to the larynx

evidence.verbatim: that production is dependent on the hormones’ essential and unique component: iodine.

canonical: The adrenal glands sit atop the kidneys and consist of an outer cortex and an inner medulla.

evidence.verbatim: Both adrenal glands sit atop the kidneys and are composed of an outer cortex and an inner medulla

canonical: The pineal gland produces and secretes melatonin, a hormone derived from serotonin.

evidence.verbatim: The pinealocyte cells that make up the pineal gland are known to produce and secrete the amine hormone melatonin , which is derived from serotonin.

canonical: Melatonin secretion varies according to the level of light received from the environment.

evidence.verbatim: The secretion of melatonin varies according to the level of light received from the environment.

canonical: Estrogens are the primary hormones produced by the ovaries.

canonical: Blood is a connective tissue made up of formed elements (cells) and a fluid extracellular matrix called plasma.

evidence.verbatim: blood is a connective tissue. Like all connective tissues, it is made up of cellular elements and an extracellular matrix.

canonical: The formed elements of blood are red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets.

evidence.verbatim: The cellular elements—referred to as the formed elements —include red blood cells (RBCs) , white blood cells (WBCs) , and cell fragments called platelets .

canonical: Hemopoiesis (hematopoiesis) is the process by which the body produces new blood cells and platelets.

evidence.verbatim: The process by which this replacement occurs is called hemopoiesis , or hematopoiesis

canonical: The erythrocyte (red blood cell) is the most common formed element in blood.

evidence.verbatim: The erythrocyte , commonly known as a red blood cell (or RBC), is by far the most common formed element

canonical: The primary function of erythrocytes is to pick up oxygen from the lungs and transport it to the body's tissues.

evidence.verbatim: The primary functions of erythrocytes are to pick up inhaled oxygen from the lungs and transport it to the body’s tissues

canonical: The leukocyte (white blood cell) is a major component of the body's defenses against disease.

evidence.verbatim: The leukocyte , commonly known as a white blood cell (or WBC), is a major component of the body’s defenses against disease.

canonical: Leukocytes are the only formed elements of blood that are complete cells, possessing a nucleus and organelles.

evidence.verbatim: they are the only formed elements that are complete cells, possessing a nucleus and organelles.

canonical: Hemostasis is the process by which the body seals a ruptured blood vessel and prevents further loss of blood.

evidence.verbatim: hemostasis , the process by which the body seals a ruptured blood vessel and prevents further loss of blood.

canonical: The three steps of hemostasis are vascular spasm, formation of a platelet plug, and coagulation (blood clotting).

evidence.verbatim: There are three steps to the process: vascular spasm, the formation of a platelet plug, and coagulation (blood clotting).

canonical: The major human blood groups were discovered by Karl Landsteiner in 1900.

evidence.verbatim: the discovery of the major human blood groups by Karl Landsteiner, an Austrian biologist and physician, in 1900.

canonical: The heart is located in the thoracic cavity, in the mediastinum between the lungs.

evidence.verbatim: The human heart is located within the thoracic cavity, medially between the lungs in the space known as the mediastinum.

canonical: Autorhythmicity is the heart's ability to initiate an electrical potential at a fixed rate that spreads from cell to cell to trigger contraction.

evidence.verbatim: its ability to initiate an electrical potential at a fixed rate that spreads rapidly from cell to cell to trigger the contractile mechanism. This property is known as autorhythmicity .

canonical: The cardiac cycle is the period that begins with contraction of the atria and ends with ventricular relaxation.

evidence.verbatim: The period of time that begins with contraction of the atria and ends with ventricular relaxation is known as the cardiac cycle

canonical: Systole is the period of cardiac contraction during which the heart pumps blood, and diastole is the period of relaxation during which the chambers fill with blood.

evidence.verbatim: The period of contraction that the heart undergoes while it pumps blood into circulation is called systole . The period of relaxation that occurs as the chambers fill with blood is called diastole .

canonical: Cardiac output is the amount of blood pumped by each ventricle in one minute, and equals heart rate multiplied by stroke volume.

evidence.verbatim: Cardiac output (CO) is a measurement of the amount of blood pumped by each ventricle in one minute. ... CO = HR × SV

canonical: The heart is the first functional organ to develop in the embryo, beginning to beat around day 21 or 22 after fertilization.

evidence.verbatim: The human heart is the first functional organ to develop. It begins beating and pumping blood around day 21 or 22, a mere three weeks after fertilization.

canonical: An artery is a blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart.

evidence.verbatim: An artery is a blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart

canonical: A vein is a blood vessel that returns blood to the heart.

evidence.verbatim: a vein, a larger blood vessel that returns blood to the heart.

canonical: Capillaries are the smallest blood vessels, where nutrients and wastes are exchanged.

evidence.verbatim: tiny capillaries, where nutrients and wastes are exchanged

canonical: Blood travels through the body in two circuits: the systemic circuit and the pulmonary circuit.

evidence.verbatim: Arteries and veins transport blood in two distinct circuits: the systemic circuit and the pulmonary circuit

canonical: Blood pressure is the force exerted by blood upon the walls of the blood vessels.

evidence.verbatim: One form of hydrostatic pressure is blood pressure , the force exerted by blood upon the walls of the blood vessels or the chambers of the heart.

canonical: Resistance is the phenomenon of factors that impede or slow blood flow.

evidence.verbatim: the factors that impede or slow blood flow, a phenomenon known as resistance .

canonical: The immune system is the complex collection of cells and organs that destroys or neutralizes pathogens that would otherwise cause disease or death.

evidence.verbatim: The immune system is the complex collection of cells and organs that destroys or neutralizes pathogens that would otherwise cause disease or death.

canonical: The lymphatic system is the system of vessels, cells, and organs that carries excess fluids to the bloodstream and filters pathogens from the blood.

evidence.verbatim: The lymphatic system is the system of vessels, cells, and organs that carries excess fluids to the bloodstream and filters pathogens from the blood.

canonical: The immune system uses two overlapping mechanisms: the innate immune response, which is rapid but nonspecific, and the adaptive immune response, which is slower but highly specific.

evidence.verbatim: the innate immune response, which is relatively rapid but nonspecific ... and the adaptive immune response, which is slower in its development ... but is highly specific

canonical: An antibody, also called an immunoglobulin, is essentially a secreted form of a B cell receptor.

evidence.verbatim: An antibody protein is essentially a secreted form of a B cell receptor.

canonical: Antigens are small chemical groups, often associated with pathogens, that are recognized by receptors on the surface of B and T lymphocytes.

evidence.verbatim: Antigens, the small chemical groups often associated with pathogens, are recognized by receptors on the surface of B and T lymphocytes.

canonical: The major functions of the respiratory system are to provide oxygen to body tissues, remove carbon dioxide, and help maintain acid-base balance.

evidence.verbatim: The major organs of the respiratory system function primarily to provide oxygen to body tissues for cellular respiration, remove the waste product carbon dioxide, and help to maintain acid-base balance.

canonical: The respiratory system is divided functionally into a conducting zone and a respiratory zone, with gas exchange occurring in the respiratory zone.

evidence.verbatim: the respiratory system can be divided into a conducting zone and a respiratory zone. ... The gas exchange occurs in the respiratory zone .

canonical: The lungs exchange respiratory gases across an epithelial surface area of about 70 square meters.

evidence.verbatim: the lungs exchange respiratory gases across a very large epithelial surface area—about 70 square meters

canonical: Pulmonary ventilation, the act of breathing, is the movement of air into and out of the lungs.

evidence.verbatim: Pulmonary ventilation is the act of breathing, which can be described as the movement of air into and out of the lungs.

canonical: Most oxygen is transported from the lungs to the body's tissues bound to hemoglobin, with only about 1.5% dissolved in the blood.

evidence.verbatim: A small amount of oxygen does dissolve in the blood ... but it is only about 1.5% of the total amount. The majority of oxygen molecules are carried from the lungs to the body’s tissues by a spe

evidence.verbatim: hyperventilation is an increased ventilation rate that is independent of the cellular oxygen needs and leads to abnormally low blood carbon dioxide levels and high (alkaline) blood pH.

canonical: The function of the digestive system is to break down food, release its nutrients, and absorb them into the body.

evidence.verbatim: The function of the digestive system is to break down the foods you eat, release their nutrients, and absorb those nutrients into the body.

canonical: The small intestine is the primary digestive organ, where most digestion and practically all absorption occur.

evidence.verbatim: Chyme released from the stomach enters the small intestine , which is the primary digestive organ in the body. Not only is this where most digestion occurs, it is also where practically all absorption occurs.

canonical: The small intestine is about 3.05 meters (10 feet) long in a living person.

evidence.verbatim: the small intestine is about 3.05 meters (10 feet) long in a living person

canonical: The empty stomach is about the size of a fist but can stretch to hold as much as 4 liters of food and fluid.

evidence.verbatim: The empty stomach is only about the size of your fist, but can stretch to hold as much as 4 liters of food and fluid

canonical: The liver is the largest gland in the body, weighing about three pounds in an adult.

evidence.verbatim: The liver is the largest gland in the body, weighing about three pounds in an adult.

canonical: The digestive role of the liver is to produce bile and export it to the duodenum, while the gallbladder stores, concentrates, and releases bile.

evidence.verbatim: The digestive role of the liver is to produce bile and export it to the duodenum. The gallbladder primarily stores, concentrates, and releases bile.

canonical: Chemical digestion breaks large food molecules into subunits small enough to be absorbed, accomplished by enzymes through hydrolysis.
